correctness.rationale: Affine plane axioms give MM^T=qI+J, full row rank, the exact five-part Laplacian spectrum (multiplicities 1, q^2-1, q, q^2-1, 1), and lower bounds q^2-1 total and q line inputs. For the proposed actuator set, selected line constraints x_P+x_Q=0 for all q omitted-line points and 1^T x=0 force x=0; selected parallel directions sample the q-dimensional line kernel injectively; constant eigenmodes are visible. Every selected black line has exactly two white point neighbors, every selected black point at least q white line neighbors. Exact standard-library checks passed for prime orders 2,3,5,7,11. The finite check is not used as proof of universal coverage.

originality.rationale: The prior zero-forcing paper supplies sufficiency and acknowledges a small converse counterexample; the maximum-multiplicity framework supplies the abstract input-channel criterion and can imply the scalar lower bound once this spectrum is known. Neither inspected source states or implies the explicit all-affine-plane coordinate placement simultaneously minimizing total and line-only actuator budgets while being zero-forcing-stalled. A projective-plane incidence graph is a different matrix with different spectral multiplicities; its exact controller count is not equivalent. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found only related but not dominating claims; remaining unindexed specialty coverage is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A broader affine-design controllability lemma might imply the explicit placement despite not appearing in the targeted search results.
The Farrugia--Sciriha 2014 PDF was not accessible for full-text exclusion.
The scalar minimum q^2-1 should not be advertised as a departure from the general maximum-multiplicity theorem; the distinct contribution is the geometric optimum and stalled zero-forcing placement.
Existing historical snapshots and indexed published-finding corpus records do not constitute complete literature coverage.

value.rationale: Determines the natural dedicated-actuator optimum for all existing affine planes, including non-Desarguesian instances, and simultaneously attains the sharp minimum number of line-side inputs with a simple geometric placement. An optimal set has no legal initial zero-forcing move, showing a substantive separation between a topology-only sufficient control certificate and fixed-Laplacian controllability. Does not claim the zero-forcing number or broad performance conclusions.
